answers.reason: A junior professor does not hold a central leadership office or senior rank required for the university senate.
University-wide budget allocation is reserved for central leadership and faculty deans.
Selecting candidates for professorships requires full professorial rank or higher office.
As a professor of the faculty, the junior professor is eligible to sit on the faculty council.
Because the junior professor teaches in the faculty, they may participate in committees preparing degree programme changes.
As a member of the professorial teaching staff, the junior professor is eligible to serve on the faculty's examination board.
Because the junior professor builds up a research group in the faculty, they may take part in the faculty's internal research funding round.
As a professor who teaches courses, the junior professor is permitted to participate in working groups revising module descriptions.
As a teaching professor with a research group, the junior professor may take part in choosing equipment for a teaching laboratory.
Holding a professorial position in the faculty allows the junior professor to take part in lower-level faculty working rounds like orientation planning.
